answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may place orders or claim rewards. When independent counterparties report a completed voyage, the protocol releases the bond; conflicting reports or proven double-spending let challengers slash it. A mirror fleet of fake accounts therefore needs separate capital for every identity and risks losing that capital if it cheats. A jetty operator can still coordinate many agents, but cannot create trusted identities for free.
